vessels.rig_words: a two-masted topsail schooner of the lakes

existence.note: No column names a vessel lying off the bar on 1 July 1835. Hubbard's editor tells of the brig Illinois lying off Chicago on 25 May 1835, unable to enter, her passengers and cargo carried ashore in Mackinaw boats; this hull stands for the vessels that waited in the offing so. Ours (L-vessels-3612).

vessels.doing: At anchor in the offing, her head to the wind, discharging into a Mackinaw boat alongside.

existence.note: Hubbard's editor: in May 1835 French Canadians carried the brig Illinois's passengers ashore in Mackinaw boats, 'which also lightered the cargo'. This boat and where she lies are ours (L-vessels-3612).

vessels.doing: Alongside the schooner in the offing, taking her cargo in for the river.

existence.note: INVENTED POSITION. Lying off the South Water bank between the merchant landings — image 11 of the 2026-08-18 brief, the South Water 1834 view, draws rowboats on this water. About 2.3 m under her; kept off the wharf decks themselves, whose record draws no vessel. Its planking (or bark), size and look are reconstructed (L-vessels-3612).

INVENTED POSITION. Her neighbour, a boat-length and a half east and swung to a different heading. About 3.1 m under her — 2.4 m until T-1630 widened this reach to Hathaway's line and put her further off the bank; she did not move — and some 24 m west of Jones's landing, which moved 9.5 m south and 1.7 m east with the bank. Its planking (or bark), size and look are reconstructed (L-vessels-3612).

vessels.title: A rowboat drawn up at the bank

existence.note: INVENTED POSITION. Drawn up at the water's edge of the South Water bank, bow to the grass — the committed ground here lies at the waterline (+0.04 m), so her stern wets and her bow rides the bank, which is what image 11 draws. The hull sits on the terrain's own surface, sampled at load. MOVED 7.3 m SOUTH by T-1630: the bank she is hauled out on came in to Hathaway's line on the owner's ruling (docs/LIBERTIES.md L275), and she was left standing in 1.9 m of open water. She keeps her easting, her heading and her relation to the waterline; only the bank moved. Its planking (or bark), size and look are reconstructed (L-vessels-3612).

vessels.title: A rowboat drawn up at the bank

existence.note: INVENTED POSITION. Beside her neighbour, a little higher up the bank on ground just proud of the water (+0.26 m) — two skiffs hauled out side by side read as a working bank, one alone reads as an accident. MOVED 8.3 m SOUTH by T-1630 with her neighbour and with the bank itself; she keeps the same step up from the waterline she was authored with. Its planking (or bark), size and look are reconstructed (L-vessels-3612).

INVENTED POSITION. A skiff lying 8 m off the west bank inside the schooner's berth, where the heightfield gives 1.2 m of water — deep for a 0.2 m draft and shoal for anything else, which is the whole reason a landing on this bank worked by boat. Nothing attests this skiff; the type is the one image 11 of the 2026-08-18 brief draws on the water at South Water Street. Its planking (or bark), size and look are reconstructed (L-vessels-3612).
